tier_reason: README carries first-party utilization tables (M1 forward 86/85/86%, fwd+bwd 62/63/64%; M3 forward 94/91/82%, fwd+bwd 71/69/61%; 4400 gigainstructions/s at 83% on M1 Max) and compares them with A100 FlashAttention-2 and H100 FlashAttention-3 utilization converted from the papers' best GFLOPS; there is no same-hardware wall-clock run against any baseline and no stated benchmark harness command or Xcode/macOS version beyond -Ounchecked, so C.

corrections.caveats: The only comparison is ALU utilization against FlashAttention-2 (A100) and FlashAttention-3 (H100) on different hardware, using the author's own gigainstruction metric; the NVIDIA side is the highest GFLOPS from each paper graph divided by 312000 (A100 SXM) or 989000 (H100 SXM), and D=256 backward entries are 0% because no result was reported. It is not a speed comparison and cannot show Apple hardware is faster in wall time; the README's 'faster than Nvidia hardware' sentence is normalized for GPU size. MFA's backward pass issues more work (7 GEMMs instead of 5), which the utilization figures partly account for via a 7/9 factor. The listed baselines (oneDNN, cuDNN, XNNPACK, Eigen tensor) and MLX/MPS/PyTorch MPS attention are not compared in the README. The derived project imperatormk/mps-flash-attention claims 1.1-4x over PyTorch SDPA on Apple Silicon; that is not evidence for this repo. Last commit 2024-09-22 (a README docs PR); last author commit 2024-08-27.

The repo has public bench code for both sides (src/main.c timing_pairing with read_tsc over 10000 iterations; baseline/ holds a blst-derived scalar build with the same gcc -O3 -march=native flags and rdtsc64.S), but the gcc version could not be confirmed without the paper, so not A.

corrections.caveats: Cycle counts and CPU (Intel Core i3-1005G1, Ice Lake) come from the TCHES/ePrint abstract seen as a WebSearch snippet; tches.iacr.org and eprint.iacr.org are blocked here (403), so the full paper (compiler version, turbo settings) was not read. The repo is public and reproducible in structure: src/main.c measures Miller loop and final exponentiation with read_tsc over 10000 iterations after a cache warm-up, and baseline/ contains a blst-derived scalar implementation (pairing.c, fp12_tower.c, assembly.S, rdtsc64.S) built with the same gcc -O3 -fomit-frame-pointer -m64 -mbmi2 -march=native -fwrapv -mtune=native flags; a verifier with paper access may raise this to A. The README states no numbers or CPU. Cycle counts on one laptop-class CPU; AVX-512 frequency effects and wall-clock time are not reported in the abstract. Baseline is blst, not GMP or MPFR, so it is outside the listed baselines. Last commit 2025-09-27.
